Effort now compares the complete allocation. For each task, compare its weight with each alternative. Differences up to10percentage points are similar; a clearly higher comparison counts+1, a clearly lower comparison-1. Positive balance is high effort, negative balance low, and zero medium. Equal weights always agree, card order is irrelevant, and graduated high/medium/low patterns are retained rather than forced into one-high or two-high groups.

The10-point similarity is an explicit game-design tolerance matching the approved near-even range. It is not an empirical threshold or a derivation from Goodhart’s Law. Categories are qualitative relative responses, not measured percentages of effort or learning. Relative boundaries still exist; small edits crossing a relative-gap boundary may change a category. The old absolute24/25 and66/67 cutoffs are gone.

Examples checked in every card order:49/26/25 and49/27/24 both high/low/low;45/45/10 high/high/low;34/33/33 all medium;65/24/11 high/medium/low. Thus24% is not intrinsically minimum effort.40/30/30→40/31/29 changes to high/medium/low while the raised31share remains medium, never decreasing its own effort.

The allocator now preserves the ratio of other unlocked shares with positive integer rounding. A no-op leaves the allocation untouched. This avoids unintentionally resetting alternatives to equal values and changing relative priorities. Locked values, total100, minimum1, maximum98 and either-card linked-pair confirmation remain.

All4851legal positive allocations are checked, including all6card permutations,28518one-point transfers and every requested slider value0through100 in every edited position. Own-share effort cannot fall when the edited share rises, including actual proportional slider updates; decreasing it cannot raise that task’s band. Zero weights and invalid totals remain rejected.

Scene shots, qualitative rows, low-task coverage ticks, teacher/Alex reviews, future prompts and comparison deltas all use the same effortAt function. WeightPattern metadata now includes mixed graduated priorities. Dialogue tests cover13200complete cross-level paths and320two/three-trial histories without repeated lines or emoji. Partner requests, copied records, names and nullable comparisons remain compatible.

All v19 presentation changes remain: no small question headings or allocation strip, shorter one-line desktop hints, explicit score-based stopping reminder and responsive wrapping. Shared attention is acknowledged while Alex’s scoring-based stopping remains a separate narrative concern across distributions, never a fabricated numerical learning loss.

Final-build browser suites exercise one-high/two-low49/26/25→49/27/24 without a24/25cliff, two-high/one-low45/45/10 with two coverage ticks, near-even and graduated patterns, first-even and first-uneven paths, two-test completion, optional-third cancellation/reopening, focus/spotlight,320/390/768/1366px layouts, visible-time pacing, custom scenes and sound. No runtime errors were found.

All four final builds and five latest ZIPs match current manifest hashes and byte comparisons. Offline packaged checks cover standalone Level1/2/3 and connected Level1→2→3; the review ZIP contains standalone Level3 and the full three-level game from those same builds. The endpoint remains theory.reveal with no Design Lab navigation.

This release supersedes the absolute effort model in v17–v19 while preserving the v18 player path and v19 copy/layout fixes. The partner’s authored animation scripts and Level1/2 gameplay are unchanged. Functional consistency checks do not establish measured learning efficacy or the best possible game design.
